sources.entry: Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures, Roy Fielding (the inventor of REST)

summary.title: Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures
summary.one_liner: Roy Fielding's 2000 PhD dissertation, which derives the REST architectural style from network-based architectural styles and shows how it applies to the Web's URI and HTTP standards.
takeaways: REST is derived step by step from simpler architectural styles (null style, client-server, stateless server, caching, uniform interface, layered system).
Network-based application styles are classified into data-flow, replication, hierarchical, mobile code, and peer-to-peer families and evaluated for hypermedia systems.
REST's architectural elements are described as data elements, connectors, and components, with process and other architectural views.
The dissertation evaluates how REST was applied to the Web's URI and HTTP standards and what lessons it draws from that experience.
summary.summary: This is the full text of Roy Fielding's 2000 doctoral dissertation from UC Irvine, arranged as a chapter-by-chapter web page. It covers software architecture fundamentals, evaluates network-based architectural styles for hypermedia, and explains the problems behind designing the Web architecture. The core chapter derives Representational State Transfer (REST) by adding constraints to a sequence of styles, then describes REST's data elements, connectors, and components. The final chapters apply REST to URI and HTTP and draw architectural lessons from that work.
